subject: EuroBank: hosting attestation and SOC 2 period alignment
messages:
From: Helen Brooks <helen.brooks@eurobank.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: EuroBank Security <security@eurobank.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Info request: SOC 2 coverage and hosting locality for EU customers

Hi Neha,

We're preparing for EuroBank's platform review and need a couple of clarifications around Redwood's SOC 2 Type II coverage and hosting boundaries. Specifically: 

- Can you confirm the date range for your latest SOC 2 Type II (start/end dates) and whether the report explicitly covers processing of data originating from EU customers?
- For hosted customers in the EU, where is the data plane (compute/storage) located (region / cloud provider)? Do you route any customer data through systems outside the EU (control plane, telemetry, logs)?
- If parts of the control plane or backups are outside the EU, do you provide a bridge letter or interim attestation to cover audit windows or cross-border evidence for our reviewers? If so, what's the standard wording and authorizing signature?
- Is customer-managed KMS supported for EU customers who require keys to be resident in the EU?

We'd like to close this by early June to align with our internal audit calendar. If helpful, a short call with your security lead would be great.

Thanks,
Helen Brooks
Senior IT Risk Manager
EuroBank

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Helen Brooks <helen.brooks@eurobank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Info request: SOC 2 coverage and hosting locality for EU customers

Hi Helen — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, full detail below and attaching a redacted copy of our SOC 2 Type II report and a simple hosting/dataflow diagram.

High level: 
- SOC 2 Type II (period): 2025-06-01 to 2026-05-31 (we've attached a redacted PDF suitable for customer review).
- Hosted data plane: For EU-hosted customers our managed compute and storage are provisioned in AWS eu-west-1 (Ireland) by default; we also support eu-west-2 (London) for UK-specific deployments.
- Control plane & telemetry: Our multi-tenant control plane metadata (account orchestration, routing) is currently operated from a dedicated control plane in us-east-1. No customer plaintext content is persisted in the US control plane; telemetry/metrics used for health/ops are aggregated and pseudonymized.
- Bridge letters / interim attestations: We can provide a signed interim attestation ("bridge letter") to clarify audit window coverage for customers whose audit windows overlap our SOC 2 period.
- KMS / keys: We support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS with BYOK options and can configure keys to be EU-resident for Dedicated or Private deployments. For self-serve hosted customers we offer envelope encryption with regional KMS where requested via an enterprise contract.

Action items / next steps: 
1) I attached: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-06-redacted.pdf and hosting-dataflow-eu-map.png.
2) Please confirm whether EuroBank requires an EU-resident control plane or if a bridge letter will be sufficient for the audit reviewers.
3) If you need a bridge letter, we can propose language and arrange sign-off from our Head of Security.

If it's helpful, Aditya can schedule a 30-min sync with your audit team next week; Marissa is cc'd and can provide the technical attestation language.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-06-redacted.pdf (redacted), hosting-dataflow-eu-map.png

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: EuroBank: hosting attestation and SOC 2 period alignment

Hi all — drafted a concise attestation and included implementation notes below. I've attached a proposed-bridge-letter-draft.docx to this thread. Please review and tell me if you'd like the Head of Security to sign it as-is or if legal wants to tweak wording.

Proposed attestation (summary):
"Redwood Inference confirms that its most recent SOC 2 Type II report covers the period June 1, 2025 through May 31, 2026. For customers who have elected EU-hosted service, our production compute and persistent storage are provisioned in AWS eu-west-1 (Ireland) and, where requested for UK residency, in AWS eu-west-2 (London). Redwood's global control plane, used for orchestration and routing, is hosted in us-east-1; the control plane does not persist customer plaintext content. Aggregated telemetry and anonymized operational logs are used for service reliability and are not sufficient to reconstruct customer content.

Where an audit window overlaps the SOC 2 period, Redwood can provide a signed interim attestation (bridge letter) clarifying the portion of the customer's activity covered by the SOC 2 report and detailing transitional compensating controls in effect for the remainder of the customer's audit window. This attestation is issued by Redwood's Head of Security and is suitable for review by customer auditors."

Implementation notes / technical caveats: 
- CMKs: customer-managed keys in AWS KMS are supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted customers we can enable regionally-scoped envelope keys upon enterprise contract and KMS configuration. For strict EU-residency of keys we recommend Dedicated or Private because of the administrative separation.
- Backups & exports: backups for EU-hosted tenants are retained in-region by default; cross-region backups are not performed unless explicitly configured. We can produce dataflow artifacts and hash-based proofs for auditors on request (see attached hosting-dataflow-eu-map.png).
- Timing: if EuroBank wants the bridge letter, we can provide a signed PDF within 3 business days after legal review.

Suggested next steps for Helen / EuroBank: 
1) Confirm whether an attestation is sufficient or if you require contract amendments to mandate an EU control plane.
2) If attestation is OK, reply to this thread and we will issue the signed bridge letter targeted to your auditor.
3) If you need CMK residency and contractual guarantees, Aditya will follow up with procurement on Dedicated/Private pricing and timeline.

Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Lead, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-bridge-letter-draft.docx
